newsitem.title: FINLAND: De La Rue says has new counterfeit detector.
newsitem.headline: De La Rue says has new counterfeit detector.

text.p: British banknote printer and security products group De La Rue Plc said on Tuesday it had launched a new system to detect counterfeit money.

De La Rue said in a statement released in conjuction with an Interpol conference here that its new system, called Kryptal, was the first internationally available standard enabling authentication of banknotes at a range of levels, reserving the highest level for central banks.
"Kryptal is a suite of machine readable features, in a single security thread, designed to maximise counterfeit banknote detection at all levels of the cash cycle," it said.
The system would enable central banks to delegate banknote sorting to commercial organisations with authentication to an approved standard without compromising security, De La Rue said.

The system could be used on a full range of cash handling machines, "from cash acceptors on car park/transport tickets up to the high speed sorting machines used in large cash sorting centres and central banks," it said.
